C0.quote: a voting rule selects a slate of k statements that is proportionally representative
C0.note: Multiwinner-style selection process aggregating agents' preferences, with proportional representation axiom (BJR). Borderline due to LLM focus but the main object is a voting process.

C1.quote: we show that, with access to polynomially many of these queries
C1.note: BJR axiom satisfiability and impossibilities (AX) plus query-complexity bounds (AL); LLM validation and survey pilot (EM); framework (OT). Axiomatic results are the largest share.

C2.1.value: utility functions (accessed via Disc queries); ratings
C2.1.quote: Each agent i ∈ N has a utility function ui : U → R

C2.2.note: Input to process is accessed through queries returning cardinal utilities; ratings on 7-point scale.

C2.3.quote: Each agent i ∈ N has a utility function ui : U → R

C2.4.note: Process is applied directly to utilities (via queries); no statement about submission or misreporting.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting; the discussion mentions malicious input only as a future hardening issue.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: Input format is cardinal only (CARD), so applicability condition not met.

C4.2.note: Approval utilities are used but not described as dichotomous preferences.

C5.1.quote: Our notion of representation expresses that agents have a claim to being represented
C5.1.note: BJR is a proportionality/representation axiom; pilot evaluates participant ratings of assigned statements.

C5.2.quote: utilities as expressing how accurately and completely the statement captures
C5.2.note: BJR and ratings are evaluated on utilities which the process uses directly; no statement relating them to a separate held attitude. Doubt vs HELD: utilities are the model's primitive and the process accesses them via queries (LLM-predicted).

VOT.note: Agents have utilities but take no action in the model; the process is queried via oracle.

ORG.note: The democratic process is an algorithm, not a modelled choosing agent.

DES.note: Designer's choice is not modelled formally.

OTH.note: The LLM acts as an oracle, not a modelled agent with its own objective.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type

claims.quote: 84 out of 100 participants feel “excellently” or “exceptionally” represented
the democratic process can tap into the power of LLMs
the vast majority of participant opinions are represented accurately by our slate

C9.1.note: Claims about representation of real participants and the process being democratic.

C9.2.quote: Hence, the vast majority of participant opinions are represented accurately by our slate.
C9.2.note: Representation claims rely on assuming ratings/utilities reflect participants' actual views (input-attitude relation) and non-strategic participation, which are not stated; the claim of democratic legitimacy also needs LLM accuracy and sincere behaviour.

C10.1.note: No statement of purely procedural reading.
